scope: Native EXR input decoding directly into a single owned RGB allocation, preserving display/data windows, RGB layer selection, chromaticities and signed/HDR samples; rejecting nonfinite RGB and missing RGB layers.
measurement_method: Separate release processes with eight Rayon workers. EXR generation completed before baseline/native measurements. /usr/bin/time -v measures peak process RSS; the decode timer excludes source/component hashing. Shared machine, one observation per completed configuration.

baseline_40mp.scope: All decoded components of an owned constant signed/HDR RGBA EXR fixture; process RSS is measured separately, not by this receipt.

native_40mp.scope: All decoded components of an owned constant signed/HDR RGBA EXR fixture; process RSS is measured separately, not by this receipt.

native_101mp.scope: All decoded components of an owned constant signed/HDR RGBA EXR fixture; process RSS is measured separately, not by this receipt.

regressions: First RGB layer after a depth layer; half-float signed/HDR with positive and negative window offsets and clipping.
Distant legal display/data window origins clip all source pixels without imposing a coordinate cap.
NaN and positive/negative infinity RGB samples are rejected with immutable input bytes.
A depth-only EXR fails both pixel import and metadata-only color-revision lookup.
Existing Rec.2020 chromaticities, source revisions and saved-layer compatibility checks pass.
Existing oriented float TIFF to Vulkan/coherent CUDA to EXR round trips preserve signed/HDR values through the new input path.
discarded_measurement: An initial 101MP decode overlapped fixture generation and correctly failed the input immutability check. It is excluded from the completed measurements; generation then finished and the final run passed.
limits: Peak RSS is process memory, not an aggregate GB10 system-memory measurement.
These are generated constant fixtures and targeted window/color/invalid-data controls, not a general photographic-quality or latency guarantee.
Existing RGB input behavior ignores alpha and crops/pads to the EXR display window; deep data and non-RGB channels remain outside this input path.
